headword: {仮設住宅|かせつじゅうたく}

definitions.explanation: Prefabricated homes put up quickly, usually by local governments, for people who lost their homes in an earthquake, flood or other disaster.

examples.japanese: {仮設住宅|かせつじゅうたく}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{住|す}む→住む：00673_sumu⟧。
⟦{被災地|ひさいち}→被災地：27434_hisaichi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{仮設住宅|かせつじゅうたく}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{建|た}てられた→建てる：01189_tateru⟧。
examples.english: Temporary housing was built in the disaster area.

examples.japanese: ⟦{震災|しんさい}→震災：14610_shinsai⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{三年|さんねん}→三年：10984_sannen⟧⟦{経|た}って→経つ：09892_tatsu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{仮設住宅|かせつじゅうたく}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{続|つづ}けて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Three years after the earthquake, many people are still living in temporary housing.

notes:
⟦{仮設|かせつ}→仮設：21123_kasetsu⟧ (temporary, provisional) + ⟦{住宅|じゅうたく}→住宅：03280_juutaku⟧ (housing). Often shortened to ⟦{仮設|かせつ}→仮設：21123_kasetsu⟧ in news and speech.

CULTURAL NOTE:
After major disasters such as the 1995 Hanshin earthquake and the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake, rows of {仮設住宅|かせつじゅうたく} became a familiar sight, and residents often stayed for years. Loneliness among the elderly living there has been reported as a social problem.
